{ .recipe-label }

- A bid well below its 5-week level means fewer dealers want the bond than usual.
- A null means no axes on that side today, or over the whole window.

## Axes in a relative-value screen

`flt_spread()`, `spread(spread_type=OAS)`
{ .recipe-uses }

Spreads next to axes: can you buy the cheap bonds, and sell the rich ones?

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
get(name, nxt_call_dt,
    flt_spread().value as #back_end,
    spread(spread_type=OAS).value as #oas,
    axes() as #ax)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE),
        crncy() == 'USD' and country_iso() == 'SE' and
        basel_iii_designation() == 'Additional Tier 1'))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(
    df.select(
        "name",
        call="nxt_call_dt",
        back_end="#back_end",
        oas=pl.col("#oas").round(0),
        bid_mm=pl.col("BID_TOTAL_SIZE") / 1e6,
        ask_mm=pl.col("ASK_TOTAL_SIZE") / 1e6,
    ).sort("oas", descending=True)
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (8, 6)
┌─────────────────┬────────────┬──────────┬───────┬────────┬────────┐
│ name            ┆ call       ┆ back_end ┆ oas   ┆ bid_mm ┆ ask_mm │
│ ---             ┆ ---        ┆ ---      ┆ ---   ┆ ---    ┆ ---    │
│ str             ┆ date       ┆ f64      ┆ f64   ┆ f64    ┆ f64    │
╞═════════════════╪════════════╪══════════╪═══════╪════════╪════════╡
│ SEB 6 ¾ PERP    ┆ 2034-06-02 ┆ 285.0    ┆ 283.0 ┆ null   ┆ 12.2   │
│ SEB 6 ¾ PERP    ┆ 2031-11-04 ┆ 312.7    ┆ 233.0 ┆ 1.0    ┆ 5.0    │
│ SWEDA 7 ¾ PERP  ┆ 2030-03-17 ┆ 365.7    ┆ 229.0 ┆ 31.0   ┆ 1.0    │
│ SHBASS 4 ¾ PERP ┆ 2031-03-01 ┆ 404.8    ┆ 228.0 ┆ 0.2    ┆ 7.6    │
│ SWEDA 4 PERP    ┆ 2029-03-17 ┆ 286.4    ┆ 198.0 ┆ 20.0   ┆ null   │
│ SEB 6 ⅞ PERP    ┆ 2027-06-30 ┆ 407.3    ┆ 196.0 ┆ 33.0   ┆ 2.0    │
│ SWEDA 7 ⅝ PERP  ┆ 2028-03-17 ┆ 358.9    ┆ 186.0 ┆ 3.0    ┆ 8.0    │
│ SHBASS 4 ⅜ PERP ┆ 2027-03-01 ┆ 394.2    ┆ 155.0 ┆ 49.0   ┆ 7.0    │
└─────────────────┴────────────┴──────────┴───────┴────────┴────────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `flt_spread()` is the back end: the margin the coupon resets to if the bond is not
  called. `#oas` is the option-adjusted spread.
- A wide OAS with ask axes is a cheap bond that dealers offer; a tight OAS with bid
  axes is a rich bond that dealers want to buy.
- Add more fields (ratings, CET1, returns) to `get()` in the same way.
  `combine(on="ID")` joins every item on the bond.

## Top 3 dealers

`axes_by_dealer()`
{ .recipe-uses }

The dealers with the most axes on these bonds, bid and ask together.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
get(axes_by_dealer())
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE),
        crncy() == 'USD' and country_iso() == 'SE' and
        basel_iii_designation() == 'Additional Tier 1'))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query)[0]
top = (
    df.group_by(dealer=pl.coalesce("BID_DEALER", "ASK_DEALER"))
    .agg(
        bonds=pl.col("ID").n_unique(),
        bid_mm=pl.col("BID_SIZE").sum() / 1e6,
        ask_mm=pl.col("ASK_SIZE").sum() / 1e6,
    )
    .with_columns(total_mm=pl.col("bid_mm") + pl.col("ask_mm"))
    .sort(["total_mm", "dealer"], descending=[True, False])
    .head(3)
)
print(top)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (3, 5)
┌────────┬───────┬────────┬────────┬──────────┐
│ dealer ┆ bonds ┆ bid_mm ┆ ask_mm ┆ total_mm │
│ ---    ┆ ---   ┆ ---    ┆ ---    ┆ ---      │
│ str    ┆ u32   ┆ f64    ┆ f64    ┆ f64      │
╞════════╪═══════╪════════╪════════╪══════════╡
│ HSBC   ┆ 4     ┆ 39.0   ┆ 0.0    ┆ 39.0     │
│ GS     ┆ 6     ┆ 10.4   ┆ 12.2   ┆ 22.6     │
│ MS     ┆ 6     ┆ 16.0   ┆ 5.0    ┆ 21.0     │
└────────┴───────┴────────┴────────┴──────────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- A dealer axed on both sides of a bond has its bid and ask on one row, so
  `coalesce()` gives one dealer per row.
- `preferences(addcols=all)` adds `BID_TIMESTAMP` and `ASK_TIMESTAMP` as UTC
  `Datetime` columns, useful for dropping axes that were not updated today.

!!! abstract "Related"
    See also `IMGR AXE <GO>`, `QMGR AXE <GO>` and `BQLX <GO>`. For how `bql()` and
    `combine()` work, see [BQL](../usage/bql.md).

Source: https://marekozana.github.io/polars-bloomberg/recipes/capital-structure/

# Bonds and Capital Structure

Which bonds and loans does a company have, how do they rank, who owns the issuer,
and how much debt sits at each level?
{ .recipe-lead }

!!! info "Data on this page"
    This page answers these questions for the three large Swedish banks, for a
    European high-yield issuer (Virgin Media O2) and for a group with several
    issuers (Heimstaden).

    Amounts are converted to EUR so that they add up across currencies. The outputs
    below are live data as of 2026-11-17 and will differ when you run the queries.
    Before you adapt a query, read the [Pitfalls](#pitfalls).

## Quick reference

=== "By task"

    | You want | Use | One row per |
    |---|---|---|
    | All live bonds of an issuer | `filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True), ticker in [...])` | bond |
    | Its loans | `filter(loansUniv(ACTIVE), ticker == '...')` | loan |
    | Where a bond ranks | `normalized_payment_rank()` (comparable across issuers), `payment_rank()` (as issued), `basel_iii_designation()` (bank capital) | bond |
    | Debt per rank, per issuer or per parent | `sum(group(amt_outstanding(currency=EUR), ...))` | group |
    | The company that owns the issuer | `parent(type=DIRECT)`, `type=ULTIMATE` or `type=CAST` | company |
    | The parent's fundamentals next to each bond | `value(<field>, parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE)` | bond |

=== "Parent types"

    The capital structure (CAST) parent is the top company of the capital structure
    you see in `CAST <GO>`. Unlike the ultimate parent, it stops below private-equity
    sponsors, owners that hold the company as an investment, and governments that
    guarantee less than half of the group's debt. Since May 2026 BQL's `parent()`
    returns it with `type=CAST`.

    | `parent(type=...)` | Returns |
    |---|---|
    | `DIRECT` (default) | the immediate parent company |
    | `ULTIMATE` | the company that ultimately controls the issuer |
    | `CAST` | the top of the capital structure in `CAST <GO>` |

## Swedish bank capital stacks

`normalized_payment_rank()`, `sum(group(..., [ticker, #rank]))`
{ .recipe-uses }

Covered bonds, senior, senior non-preferred, Tier 2 and AT1 outstanding for SEB,
Handelsbanken and Swedbank, in EUR billions.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#rank = normalized_payment_rank().value;
    #amt = group(amt_outstanding(currency=EUR).value / 1B, [ticker, #rank]);)
get(sum(#amt) as #eur_bn)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['SEB', 'SHBASS', 'SWEDA']))
"""
layers = {
    "Secured": "1 Secured (covered)",
    "Sr Unsecured": "2 Senior preferred",
    "Senior Bail-In": "3 Senior non-preferred",
    "Subordinated Unsecured": "4 Tier 2",
    "Jr Subordinated Unsecured": "5 AT1",
}
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
print(
    df.with_columns(
        layer=pl.col("#RANK").replace(layers), eur_bn=pl.col("#eur_bn").round(1)
    )
    .pivot(on="TICKER", index="layer", values="eur_bn")
    .sort("layer")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (5, 4)
┌────────────────────────┬──────┬────────┬───────┐
│ layer                  ┆ SEB  ┆ SHBASS ┆ SWEDA │
│ ---                    ┆ ---  ┆ ---    ┆ ---   │
│ str                    ┆ f64  ┆ f64    ┆ f64   │
╞════════════════════════╪══════╪════════╪═══════╡
│ 1 Secured (covered)    ┆ 32.0 ┆ 56.8   ┆ 36.8  │
│ 2 Senior preferred     ┆ 11.7 ┆ 27.0   ┆ 14.3  │
│ 3 Senior non-preferred ┆ 12.0 ┆ 7.6    ┆ 12.5  │
│ 4 Tier 2               ┆ 2.8  ┆ 2.3    ┆ 2.8   │
│ 5 AT1                  ┆ 1.9  ┆ 1.4    ┆ 1.5   │
└────────────────────────┴──────┴────────┴───────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    Swedish banks also issue structured notes and MTNs under the same ticker, so the
    senior preferred counts are large.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `normalized_payment_rank()` maps each bond to one ladder, the same for all issuers.
  `Senior Bail-In` is senior non-preferred (MREL), `Subordinated` is Tier 2 and
  `Jr Subordinated` is AT1.
- The group column comes back as `#RANK` (upper case) and the ticker as `TICKER`.
- `consolidateduplicates=True` keeps one line per bond instead of one per listing.

## AT1 and Tier 2 call schedule

`basel_iii_designation()`, `nxt_call_dt`
{ .recipe-uses }

How much AT1 and Tier 2 each bank can call per year, in EUR millions.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
get(ticker, basel_iii_designation, nxt_call_dt,
    amt_outstanding(currency=EUR).value / 1M as #eur_m)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['SEB', 'SHBASS', 'SWEDA'] and
           basel_iii_designation() in ['Additional Tier 1', 'Tier 2']))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
tier = pl.col("basel_iii_designation").replace(
    {"Additional Tier 1": "AT1", "Tier 2": "T2"}
)
print(
    df.with_columns(
        bank_tier=pl.col("ticker") + " " + tier,
        call_year=pl.col("nxt_call_dt").dt.year(),
        eur_m=pl.col("#eur_m").round().cast(pl.Int64),
    )
    .sort("bank_tier")
    .pivot(on="bank_tier", index="call_year", values="eur_m", aggregate_function="sum")
    .sort("call_year")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (7, 7)
┌───────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────────┬───────────┬───────────┬──────────┐
│ call_year ┆ SEB AT1 ┆ SEB T2 ┆ SHBASS AT1 ┆ SHBASS T2 ┆ SWEDA AT1 ┆ SWEDA T2 │
│ ---       ┆ ---     ┆ ---    ┆ ---        ┆ ---       ┆ ---       ┆ ---      │
│ i32       ┆ i64     ┆ i64    ┆ i64        ┆ i64       ┆ i64       ┆ i64      │
╞═══════════╪═════════╪════════╪════════════╪═══════════╪═══════════╪══════════╡
│ 2027      ┆ 466     ┆ 0      ┆ 424        ┆ 594       ┆ 0         ┆ 1258     │
│ 2028      ┆ 0       ┆ 842    ┆ 0          ┆ 500       ┆ 472       ┆ 393      │
│ 2029      ┆ 439     ┆ 500    ┆ 0          ┆ 750       ┆ 425       ┆ 0        │
│ 2030      ┆ 0       ┆ 411    ┆ 0          ┆ 0         ┆ 607       ┆ 500      │
│ 2031      ┆ 459     ┆ 0      ┆ 975        ┆ 500       ┆ 0         ┆ 675      │
│ 2032      ┆ 0       ┆ 1007   ┆ 0          ┆ 0         ┆ 0         ┆ 0        │
│ 2034      ┆ 516     ┆ 0      ┆ 0          ┆ 0         ┆ 0         ┆ 0        │
└───────────┴─────────┴────────┴────────────┴───────────┴───────────┴──────────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `nxt_call_dt` is the next call date. AT1s are perpetual, so the call date is the
  date that matters.
- `basel_iii_designation()` is the regulatory tier, a better filter for bank capital
  than the payment rank.

## AT1 distance to trigger

`value(..., parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE)`, `capital_type_coco_trigger_level()`
{ .recipe-uses }

The USD AT1s of the Swedish banks (the bonds on the [Dealer Axes](axes.md) page),
each with its bank's CET1 ratio and the bond's trigger, in percent of risk-weighted
assets.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#cet1 = value(bs_tier1_com_equity_ratio(), parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE);
    #trigger = capital_type_coco_trigger_level();)
get(name, nxt_call_dt, #cet1, #trigger)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['SEB', 'SHBASS', 'SWEDA'] and crncy() == 'USD' and
           basel_iii_designation() == 'Additional Tier 1'))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(
    df.select(
        "name",
        "nxt_call_dt",
        "PERIOD_END_DATE",
        "#cet1",
        "#trigger",
        buffer_pp=pl.col("#cet1") - pl.col("#trigger"),
    ).sort("name", "nxt_call_dt")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (8, 6)
┌─────────────────┬─────────────┬─────────────────┬───────┬──────────┬───────────┐
│ name            ┆ nxt_call_dt ┆ PERIOD_END_DATE ┆ #cet1 ┆ #trigger ┆ buffer_pp │
│ ---             ┆ ---         ┆ ---             ┆ ---   ┆ ---      ┆ ---       │
│ str             ┆ date        ┆ date            ┆ f64   ┆ f64      ┆ f64       │
╞═════════════════╪═════════════╪═════════════════╪═══════╪══════════╪═══════════╡
│ SEB 6 ¾ PERP    ┆ 2031-11-04  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.1  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 11.975    │
│ SEB 6 ¾ PERP    ┆ 2034-06-02  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.1  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 11.975    │
│ SEB 6 ⅞ PERP    ┆ 2027-06-30  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.1  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 11.975    │
│ SHBASS 4 ¾ PERP ┆ 2031-03-01  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.0  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 11.875    │
│ SHBASS 4 ⅜ PERP ┆ 2027-03-01  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.0  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 11.875    │
│ SWEDA 4 PERP    ┆ 2029-03-17  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.2  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 12.075    │
│ SWEDA 7 ¾ PERP  ┆ 2030-03-17  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.2  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 12.075    │
│ SWEDA 7 ⅝ PERP  ┆ 2028-03-17  ┆ 2026-09-30      ┆ 17.2  ┆ 5.125    ┆ 12.075    │
└─────────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────────┴───────┴──────────┴───────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    The projected item adds `SOURCE_ID`, the parent's ID. Join on `ID`, or the rows of
    the two items do not match.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `value(..., parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE)` reads the field from each bond's
  capital structure parent, here the listed bank. `PERIOD_END_DATE` is the reporting
  quarter of the CET1 ratio.
- For CET1 against the full capital requirement, see the
  [Bank CET1 Ratio vs Requirements](../examples/credit/bank-CET1-vs-requirements.ipynb)
  example.

## Bonds and loans with leverage

`loansUniv(ACTIVE)`, `ebitda(fpt=LTM)`
{ .recipe-uses }

The whole debt stack of Virgin Media O2, bonds and term loans, by rank. Leverage is
the debt up to and including each rank divided by last-twelve-months EBITDA.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

fields = """
get(name, maturity, normalized_payment_rank().value as #rank,
    amt_outstanding(currency=EUR).value / 1M as #eur_m)
"""
bonds = "for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True), ticker == 'VMED'))"
loans = "for(filter(loansUniv(ACTIVE), ticker == 'VMED' and amt_outstanding() > 0))"
parent = """
get(name, ebitda(fpt=LTM, currency=EUR) / 1M as #ebitda)
for(parent('ZO388622 Corp', type=CAST))
"""
seniority = {"1st Lien Secured": 1, "Secured": 2, "Sr Unsecured": 3}
with BQuery() as bq:
    debt = pl.concat(
        [
            bq.bql(fields + bonds).combine().with_columns(kind=pl.lit("bond")),
            bq.bql(fields + loans).combine().with_columns(kind=pl.lit("loan")),
        ]
    )
    group = bq.bql(parent).combine()
ebitda = group["#ebitda"].item()
print(
    f"{group['name'].item()}: LTM EBITDA EUR {ebitda:,.0f}m ({group['PERIOD_END_DATE'].item()})"
)
print(
    debt.group_by("#rank")
    .agg(
        bonds=(pl.col("kind") == "bond").sum(),
        loans=(pl.col("kind") == "loan").sum(),
        eur_m=pl.col("#eur_m").sum().round().cast(pl.Int64),
    )
    .sort(pl.col("#rank").replace_strict(seniority, default=9))
    .with_columns(cum_leverage=(pl.col("eur_m").cum_sum() / ebitda).round(1))
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
Vmed O2 UK Ltd: LTM EBITDA EUR 3,186m (2025-12-31)
shape: (3, 5)
┌──────────────────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬──────────────┐
│ #rank            ┆ bonds ┆ loans ┆ eur_m ┆ cum_leverage │
│ ---              ┆ ---   ┆ ---   ┆ ---   ┆ ---          │
│ str              ┆ u32   ┆ u32   ┆ i64   ┆ f64          │
╞══════════════════╪═══════╪═══════╪═══════╪══════════════╡
│ 1st Lien Secured ┆ 5     ┆ 15    ┆ 18972 ┆ 6.0          │
│ Secured          ┆ 12    ┆ 0     ┆ 10120 ┆ 9.1          │
│ Sr Unsecured     ┆ 2     ┆ 0     ┆ 1314  ┆ 9.5          │
└──────────────────┴───────┴───────┴───────┴──────────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - Put the currency on the item, `ebitda(..., currency=EUR)`, or use
      `with(currency=EUR)`. `with(ccy=EUR)` is ignored without an error, and the numbers
      stay in the reporting currency. Check the `CURRENCY` column.
    - The order comes from Bloomberg's normalized rank. Read it as a debt stack, not a
      legal waterfall: debt of neighbouring ranks can share the same collateral.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `parent('ZO388622 Corp', type=CAST)` turns one bond into its group, Vmed O2 UK Ltd,
  whose accounts cover all the issuing entities.
- Private groups report less often; `PERIOD_END_DATE` shows which accounts you got.
- `loans()` on the parent returns nothing for this group, so the loans come from
  `loansUniv(ACTIVE)` by ticker. `amt_outstanding() > 0` drops repaid and undrawn
  facilities.
- Some `VMED` bonds are vendor-financing notes issued by separate vehicles. Use
  `issuer()` to see the issuing entity of each bond.

## Direct, ultimate and CAST parent

`parent(type=DIRECT)`, `ULTIMATE`, `CAST`
{ .recipe-uses }

Heimstaden has two bond issuers: Heimstaden AB and its residential subsidiary
Heimstaden Bostad. The three parent types answer "who owns this?" differently.

```python
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
get(name, issuer(),
    value(name, parent(type=DIRECT), mapby=LINEAGE) as #direct,
    value(name, parent(type=ULTIMATE), mapby=LINEAGE) as #ultimate,
    value(name, parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE) as #cast)
for(['BJ158441 Corp', 'BR871064 Corp'])
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(df.select("ID", "name", "issuer()", "#direct", "#ultimate", "#cast"))
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (2, 6)
┌───────────────┬─────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────┐
│ ID            ┆ name                ┆ issuer()             ┆ #direct              ┆ #ultimate            ┆ #cast         │
│ ---           ┆ ---                 ┆ ---                  ┆ ---                  ┆ ---                  ┆ ---           │
│ str           ┆ str                 ┆ str                  ┆ str                  ┆ str                  ┆ str           │
╞═══════════════╪═════════════════════╪══════════════════════╪══════════════════════╪══════════════════════╪═══════════════╡
│ BJ158441 Corp ┆ HEIBOS 2.8 05/04/35 ┆ HEIMSTADEN BOSTAD AB ┆ Heimstaden Bostad AB ┆ Heimstaden Bostad AB ┆ Heimstaden AB │
│ BR871064 Corp ┆ HEIMST 6 ¾ PERP     ┆ HEIMSTADEN AB        ┆ Fredensborg AS       ┆ Fredensborg 1994 AS  ┆ Heimstaden AB │
└───────────────┴─────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴───────────────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- For the Heimstaden AB bond the ultimate parent is its owner, Fredensborg. The CAST
  parent stays at Heimstaden AB, the top of the capital structure.
- For the Heimstaden Bostad bond the CAST parent is Heimstaden AB, which
  consolidates Bostad. Both issuers belong to one capital structure.
- `for(parent('BJ158441 Corp', type=CAST))` makes the parent the universe, so you
  can ask for its fundamentals directly.

## One capital structure, several issuers

`group(..., [#cast, ticker, #rank])`
{ .recipe-uses }

All Heimstaden bonds grouped by CAST parent, issuer ticker and rank, in EUR
millions.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#cast = value(name, parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE);
    #rank = normalized_payment_rank().value;
    #amt = group(amt_outstanding(currency=EUR).value / 1M, [#cast, ticker, #rank]);)
get(sum(#amt) as #eur_m, count(#amt) as #bonds)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['HEIBOS', 'HEIMST', 'HEMVLR']))
preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
print(
    df.select(
        "#CAST",
        "TICKER",
        "#RANK",
        "#bonds",
        eur_m=pl.col("#eur_m").round().cast(pl.Int64),
    ).sort("TICKER", "#RANK")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (5, 5)
┌───────────────┬────────┬───────────────────────────┬────────┬───────┐
│ #CAST         ┆ TICKER ┆ #RANK                     ┆ #bonds ┆ eur_m │
│ ---           ┆ ---    ┆ ---                       ┆ ---    ┆ ---   │
│ str           ┆ str    ┆ str                       ┆ i64    ┆ i64   │
╞═══════════════╪════════╪═══════════════════════════╪════════╪═══════╡
│ Heimstaden AB ┆ HEIBOS ┆ Jr Subordinated Unsecured ┆ 5      ┆ 3000  │
│ Heimstaden AB ┆ HEIBOS ┆ Sr Unsecured              ┆ 20     ┆ 5036  │
│ Heimstaden AB ┆ HEIMST ┆ Jr Subordinated Unsecured ┆ 2      ┆ 730   │
│ Heimstaden AB ┆ HEIMST ┆ Sr Unsecured              ┆ 3      ┆ 895   │
│ Heimstaden AB ┆ HEMVLR ┆ Sr Unsecured              ┆ 3      ┆ 74    │
└───────────────┴────────┴───────────────────────────┴────────┴───────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - `bonds('<company>')` returns the bonds of that company only, not of its
      subsidiaries, so start from the tickers and let `#cast` show what belongs
      together.
    - `dropCols=['ORIG_IDS']` matters: a group with one bond carries `ORIG_IDS` in
      `count()` but not in `sum()`, and the two items would not join.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `Jr Subordinated` here are hybrid bonds, which rank below all senior debt of the
  same issuer. Heimstaden AB's debt is also structurally below Bostad's, because
  Heimstaden AB is a holding company.

## Largest capital structures in a high-yield index

`sum(group(..., #cast))` over `members()`
{ .recipe-uses }

The ten CAST parents with the most debt in the Bloomberg Pan-European High Yield
index, with their share of the index.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#cast = value(name, parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE);
    #amt = group(amt_outstanding(currency=EUR).value / 1B, #cast);)
get(sum(#amt) as #eur_bn, count(#amt) as #bonds)
for(members('LP01TREU Index'))
preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(
    df.select(
        "#CAST",
        "#bonds",
        eur_bn=pl.col("#eur_bn").round(1),
        share_pct=(100 * pl.col("#eur_bn") / pl.col("#eur_bn").sum()).round(1),
    )
    .filter(pl.col("#CAST").is_not_null())
    .sort("eur_bn", descending=True)
    .head(10)
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (10, 4)
┌────────────────────────────────┬────────┬────────┬───────────┐
│ #CAST                          ┆ #bonds ┆ eur_bn ┆ share_pct │
│ ---                            ┆ ---    ┆ ---    ┆ ---       │
│ str                            ┆ i64    ┆ f64    ┆ f64       │
╞════════════════════════════════╪════════╪════════╪═══════════╡
│ SoftBank Group Corp            ┆ 15     ┆ 8.7    ┆ 2.1       │
│ Kemble Water Holdings Ltd      ┆ 17     ┆ 8.5    ┆ 2.0       │
│ Vmed O2 UK Ltd                 ┆ 11     ┆ 7.9    ┆ 1.9       │
│ INA-Holding Schaeffler GmbH &  ┆ 11     ┆ 6.8    ┆ 1.6       │
│ Telefonica SA                  ┆ 7      ┆ 6.6    ┆ 1.6       │
│ Maya SAS/Paris France          ┆ 10     ┆ 6.2    ┆ 1.5       │
│ Bayer AG                       ┆ 7      ┆ 6.0    ┆ 1.5       │
│ Optics Holdco Srl              ┆ 8      ┆ 5.8    ┆ 1.4       │
│ Zeppelin-Stiftung Ferdinand Gm ┆ 8      ┆ 5.6    ┆ 1.4       │
│ Next Alt Sarl                  ┆ 9      ┆ 5.5    ┆ 1.3       │
└────────────────────────────────┴────────┴────────┴───────────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- Grouping by CAST parent adds up holding companies, operating companies and
  finance vehicles of one group, which a ticker would split.
- Bonds without a CAST parent fall into one `NullGroup` row with a null `#CAST`.
  The filter removes it after the share is computed.
- `combine(on="ID")` joins the two items once; the second `#CAST` column is kept as
  `#CAST_#bonds`.

## Pitfalls

What surprised us while writing these recipes.

<div class="recipe-pitfalls" markdown>

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A bond appears on two rows after `combine()` | `mapby=LINEAGE` adds `SOURCE_ID`, which differs between items | `combine(on="ID")`, or `preferences(dropCols=['SOURCE_ID'])` |
| Thousands of rows from a parent universe | A security without a parent returns the ID `NULL_ID`, a string that matches itself in every join | Drop `NULL_ID` rows before combining, or keep one item |
| Fundamentals in GBP or SEK although you asked for EUR | `with(ccy=EUR)` leaves them in the reporting currency, without an error | `with(currency=EUR)` or `field(currency=EUR)`; check `CURRENCY` |
| `bonds('<parent>')` misses the subsidiaries' bonds | `bonds()` does not follow the CAST group: Heimstaden AB's list has no Heimstaden Bostad bonds | Start from tickers or an index and group by `parent(type=CAST)` |
| Screening all bonds of a country by CAST parent times out | The parent is looked up for every bond in the universe | Narrow the universe first (tickers, an index), then group |
| Grouped items do not line up | One-bond groups carry `ORIG_IDS` in some items only | `preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])` |

</div>

---

Source: https://marekozana.github.io/polars-bloomberg/recipes/spreads/

# Spread Statistics

How wide are spreads for each rating? How much more does an AT1 pay than a bond
with the same rating? Is the market wider than last month? And what spread does a
bond have at the price you are about to pay?
{ .recipe-lead }

BQL answers the first three for a whole index in one request: it groups the bonds'
spreads and sends back only the statistics. The last one is the YAS calculator
(`YAS <GO>`), which BQL runs at any price and workout you give it.

!!! info "Data on this page"
    Spreads are in basis points, yields in percent. The outputs below are live data
    as of 2026-11-17 and will differ when you run the queries. Before you adapt a
    query, read the [Pitfalls](#pitfalls).

## Quick reference

=== "By task"

    | You want | Use | One row per |
    |---|---|---|
    | Count, median and quartiles of spreads per rating | `count()`, `median()`, `quantile(..., 0.75)` of `group(spread(...), by=[bb_composite(), ...])` | group |
    | The same statistics month by month | `spread(dates=range(-6M, 0D), per=M)`, grouped by `year()` and `month()` of its `DATE` | group and month |
    | One number per day for all bonds of an index | `avg(group(#s, by=#s().DATE))` | day |
    | An index's own yield and spread | `yield(yield_type=YTW, universe_type=PROJECTED)`, `spread(spread_type=OAS_SOVEREIGN, universe_type=RETURNS)` | date |
    | Spread or yield at your price, to call, maturity or a date | `spread(price=..., workout=TO_NEXT_CALL)`, `TO_MATURITY`, `TO_WORST`, `TO_CUSTOM` | bond |
    | Discount margin of a floating rate note | `discount_margin(price=...)` | bond |

=== "Spread types"

    | `spread_type=` | Spread | Works for |
    |---|---|---|
    | `Z` (the default) | Z-spread: constant spread over the swap zero curve | bonds, indices |
    | `OAS` | option-adjusted spread | bonds |
    | `G`, `I`, `ASW` | over government yields, over swap rates, asset swap | bonds |
    | `OAS_SOVEREIGN`, `OAS_SWAP` | index OAS over government or swap curve | indices |

!!! warning "Name the spread type"
    `spread()` without `spread_type` is the Z-spread, not the OAS, so every recipe
    names the type.

## OAS by rating: AT1 vs other bonds

`median()`, `quantile()`, `group(..., by=[bb_composite(), ...])`
{ .recipe-uses }

Count, median and upper quartile OAS per rating from BBB+ to BB-, for AT1s (CoCos) and
for all other bonds of three European indices: Bloomberg Contingent Capital Western
Europe (`I31095`), Pan-European High Yield (`LP01STAT`) and Pan-European Aggregate
Corporate (`LP05STAT`).

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#is_coco = if(capital_contingent_security(), true, false);
    #oas = group(spread(spread_type=OAS), by=[bb_composite(), #is_coco]);)
get(count(#oas) as #n, median(#oas) as #median, quantile(#oas, 0.75) as #q3)
for(filter(members(['I31095 Index', 'LP01STAT Index', 'LP05STAT Index']),
           bb_composite() in ['BBB+', 'BBB', 'BBB-', 'BB+', 'BB', 'BB-']))
preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])
"""
ratings = pl.Enum(["BBB+", "BBB", "BBB-", "BB+", "BB", "BB-"])
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
stats = df.select(
    rating=pl.col("BB_COMPOSITE()").cast(ratings),
    at1="#IS_COCO",
    n="#n",
    median=pl.col("#median").round().cast(pl.Int64),
    q3=pl.col("#q3").round().cast(pl.Int64),
)
print(
    stats.filter(~pl.col("at1"))
    .drop("at1")
    .join(stats.filter(pl.col("at1")).drop("at1"), on="rating", suffix="_at1")
    .with_columns(premium=pl.col("median_at1") - pl.col("median"))
    .sort("rating")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (6, 8)
┌────────┬──────┬────────┬─────┬───────┬────────────┬────────┬─────────┐
│ rating ┆ n    ┆ median ┆ q3  ┆ n_at1 ┆ median_at1 ┆ q3_at1 ┆ premium │
│ ---    ┆ ---  ┆ ---    ┆ --- ┆ ---   ┆ ---        ┆ ---    ┆ ---     │
│ enum   ┆ i64  ┆ i64    ┆ i64 ┆ i64   ┆ i64        ┆ i64    ┆ i64     │
╞════════╪══════╪════════╪═════╪═══════╪════════════╪════════╪═════════╡
│ BBB+   ┆ 1043 ┆ 96     ┆ 131 ┆ 3     ┆ 228        ┆ 256    ┆ 132     │
│ BBB    ┆ 695  ┆ 92     ┆ 122 ┆ 21    ┆ 229        ┆ 269    ┆ 137     │
│ BBB-   ┆ 385  ┆ 107    ┆ 147 ┆ 92    ┆ 259        ┆ 287    ┆ 152     │
│ BB+    ┆ 172  ┆ 129    ┆ 170 ┆ 44    ┆ 257        ┆ 288    ┆ 128     │
│ BB     ┆ 106  ┆ 149    ┆ 202 ┆ 37    ┆ 285        ┆ 325    ┆ 136     │
│ BB-    ┆ 102  ┆ 161    ┆ 247 ┆ 5     ┆ 252        ┆ 270    ┆ 91      │
└────────┴──────┴────────┴─────┴───────┴────────────┴────────┴─────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    `if(capital_contingent_security(), true, false)` matters. The flag itself is
    null for most bonds that are not CoCos, their groups get a null key, and
    `combine()` cannot join them (see [Pitfalls](#pitfalls)).

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `n` is the number of bonds, `median` and `q3` the 50th and 75th percentile OAS
  of the group. Columns ending in `_at1` are the AT1s. `premium` is how much wider
  the median AT1 is than the median bond of the same rating.
- A group column is named after its expression in upper case: `BB_COMPOSITE()`,
  `#IS_COCO`. The `ID` column holds the whole group key, such as `BB+:true`.
- `bb_composite()` is today's rating. For a box plot, add `quantile(#oas, 0.25)`
  for the box and `quantile(#oas, 0.05)`, `quantile(#oas, 0.95)` for the whiskers.
- For the AT1 premium per rating over ten years, with charts, see the
  [AT1 vs Credits OAS per Rating](../examples/credit/at1-vs-credits-oas.ipynb)
  example.

## Median OAS by rating, month by month

`per=M`, `month()`, `year()`
{ .recipe-uses }

Median OAS at the last six month-ends and today, for the ratings around the line
between investment grade and high yield, in the Pan-European High Yield and
Aggregate Corporate indices. `crossover` is BB+ minus BBB-: the extra spread for
one notch below investment grade.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#oas = spread(spread_type=OAS, dates=range(-6M, 0D), per=M, fill=PREV);
    #year = year(#oas().DATE);
    #month = month(#oas().DATE);
    #median = median(group(#oas, by=[bb_composite(), #year, #month]));)
get(#median)
for(filter(members(['LP01STAT Index', 'LP05STAT Index']),
           bb_composite() in ['BBB', 'BBB-', 'BB+', 'BB']))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
print(
    df.drop_nulls("DATE")
    .pivot(on="BB_COMPOSITE()", index="DATE", values="#median")
    .sort("DATE")
    .select(
        "DATE",
        pl.col("BBB", "BBB-", "BB+", "BB").round(),
        crossover=(pl.col("BB+") - pl.col("BBB-")).round(),
    )
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (7, 6)
┌────────────┬──────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────────┐
│ DATE       ┆ BBB  ┆ BBB-  ┆ BB+   ┆ BB    ┆ crossover │
│ ---        ┆ ---  ┆ ---   ┆ ---   ┆ ---   ┆ ---       │
│ date       ┆ f64  ┆ f64   ┆ f64   ┆ f64   ┆ f64       │
╞════════════╪══════╪═══════╪═══════╪═══════╪═══════════╡
│ 2026-05-29 ┆ 81.0 ┆ 98.0  ┆ 120.0 ┆ 151.0 ┆ 22.0      │
│ 2026-06-30 ┆ 81.0 ┆ 95.0  ┆ 121.0 ┆ 146.0 ┆ 25.0      │
│ 2026-07-31 ┆ 78.0 ┆ 91.0  ┆ 114.0 ┆ 129.0 ┆ 23.0      │
│ 2026-08-31 ┆ 77.0 ┆ 90.0  ┆ 105.0 ┆ 118.0 ┆ 15.0      │
│ 2026-09-30 ┆ 82.0 ┆ 94.0  ┆ 128.0 ┆ 149.0 ┆ 33.0      │
│ 2026-10-30 ┆ 93.0 ┆ 106.0 ┆ 145.0 ┆ 172.0 ┆ 39.0      │
│ 2026-11-17 ┆ 92.0 ┆ 107.0 ┆ 129.0 ┆ 149.0 ┆ 21.0      │
└────────────┴──────┴───────┴───────┴───────┴───────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - `per=M` gives the last business day of each month and the latest close.
      `frq=M` instead steps back from today in whole months: run it on the 17th and
      every row is the 17th.
    - `members()` is today's index. Bonds that have left the index are missing from the
      history, and new issues count only from their issue date. Add
      `count(group(...))` to see how many bonds each median uses.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `year()` and `month()` of `#oas().DATE` put the period into the group key, so
  each rating gets one median per month.
- A bond without any spread history falls into a group whose date is null.
  `drop_nulls("DATE")` removes that row.
- `fill=PREV` carries the last spread forward over days without a price.
- For AT1 vs other bonds per rating since 2014, see the
  [AT1 vs Credits OAS per Rating](../examples/credit/at1-vs-credits-oas.ipynb)
  example.

## Daily average Z-spread of index members

`avg(group(#s, by=#s().DATE))`
{ .recipe-uses }

The average and median Z-spread of the bonds in the Bloomberg European Banks CoCo
Tier 1 index (`I31415`), for each business day of the last two weeks, with the
daily change of the average.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#z = spread(spread_type=Z, dates=range(-14D, 0D));
    #day = #z().DATE;
    #avg = avg(group(#z, by=#day));
    #median = median(group(#z, by=#day));
    #n = count(group(#z, by=#day));)
get(#avg, #median, #n)
for(members('I31415 Index'))
preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
print(
    df.filter(pl.col("#n") > 0)
    .sort("DATE")
    .select(
        "DATE",
        bonds="#n",
        avg=pl.col("#avg").round(1),
        median=pl.col("#median").round(1),
        change=pl.col("#avg").diff().round(1),
    )
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (10, 5)
┌────────────┬───────┬───────┬────────┬────────┐
│ DATE       ┆ bonds ┆ avg   ┆ median ┆ change │
│ ---        ┆ ---   ┆ ---   ┆ ---    ┆ ---    │
│ date       ┆ i64   ┆ f64   ┆ f64    ┆ f64    │
╞════════════╪═══════╪═══════╪════════╪════════╡
│ 2026-11-03 ┆ 232   ┆ 291.0 ┆ 284.6  ┆ null   │
│ 2026-11-04 ┆ 232   ┆ 287.0 ┆ 282.4  ┆ -4.0   │
│ 2026-11-05 ┆ 234   ┆ 288.1 ┆ 285.5  ┆ 1.1    │
│ 2026-11-06 ┆ 234   ┆ 288.8 ┆ 284.8  ┆ 0.7    │
│ 2026-11-09 ┆ 225   ┆ 274.2 ┆ 270.7  ┆ -14.6  │
│ 2026-11-10 ┆ 234   ┆ 263.1 ┆ 259.0  ┆ -11.1  │
│ 2026-11-11 ┆ 139   ┆ 261.1 ┆ 258.9  ┆ -2.0   │
│ 2026-11-12 ┆ 235   ┆ 259.4 ┆ 255.1  ┆ -1.7   │
│ 2026-11-13 ┆ 235   ┆ 265.0 ┆ 260.0  ┆ 5.6    │
│ 2026-11-16 ┆ 235   ┆ 270.5 ┆ 264.8  ┆ 5.4    │
└────────────┴───────┴───────┴────────┴────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - `bonds` is the number of bonds with a spread that day. Weekends, and today until
      the close is stored, have none and are dropped. On a holiday in one market fewer
      bonds are priced, and the average moves because the set of bonds changed; check
      `bonds` before you read `change` as a market move.
    - `preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])` is needed here: `ORIG_IDS` is null in every
      row, and the three items would not join.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `#z().DATE` is the date of each spread. Grouping by it gives one value per day
  for all bonds together.
- This is an equal-weighted average. The index's own spread is weighted by market
  value; the next recipe gets it.

## Index yield and spread, week by week

`universe_type`, `per=W`
{ .recipe-uses }

Yield to worst and OAS of the Bloomberg Contingent Capital EUR index (`I30904EU`)
at each Friday close for the last eight weeks. `rates` is the yield minus the
spread: what is left once the credit spread is taken out, mostly the government
bond yield. `spread_pct` is the spread's share of the yield, in percent.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#ytw = yield(yield_type=YTW, universe_type=PROJECTED);
    #oas = spread(spread_type=OAS_SOVEREIGN, universe_type=RETURNS);)
get(#ytw, #oas)
for(['I30904EU Index'])
with(dates=range(-8W, 0D), per=W, fill=PREV)
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
oas_pct = pl.col("#oas") / 100
print(
    df.select(
        "DATE",
        ytw=pl.col("#ytw").round(2),
        oas_bp=pl.col("#oas").round(),
        rates=(pl.col("#ytw") - oas_pct).round(2),
        spread_pct=(100 * oas_pct / pl.col("#ytw")).round(),
    )
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (9, 5)
┌────────────┬──────┬────────┬───────┬────────────┐
│ DATE       ┆ ytw  ┆ oas_bp ┆ rates ┆ spread_pct │
│ ---        ┆ ---  ┆ ---    ┆ ---   ┆ ---        │
│ date       ┆ f64  ┆ f64    ┆ f64   ┆ f64        │
╞════════════╪══════╪════════╪═══════╪════════════╡
│ 2026-09-25 ┆ 5.97 ┆ 248.0  ┆ 3.5   ┆ 41.0       │
│ 2026-10-02 ┆ 6.3  ┆ 297.0  ┆ 3.33  ┆ 47.0       │
│ 2026-10-09 ┆ 6.12 ┆ 279.0  ┆ 3.33  ┆ 46.0       │
│ 2026-10-16 ┆ 6.01 ┆ 274.0  ┆ 3.27  ┆ 46.0       │
│ 2026-10-23 ┆ 6.33 ┆ 303.0  ┆ 3.3   ┆ 48.0       │
│ 2026-10-30 ┆ 6.21 ┆ 296.0  ┆ 3.26  ┆ 48.0       │
│ 2026-11-06 ┆ 6.05 ┆ 287.0  ┆ 3.18  ┆ 47.0       │
│ 2026-11-13 ┆ 6.01 ┆ 270.0  ┆ 3.31  ┆ 45.0       │
│ 2026-11-17 ┆ 6.04 ┆ 273.0  ┆ 3.32  ┆ 45.0       │
└────────────┴──────┴────────┴───────┴────────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - Index analytics need `universe_type`; without it, `yield()` and `spread()`
      return null. `PROJECTED` is the index as it will be after the next rebalancing,
      `RETURNS` the index fixed for this month's returns. Yield to worst accepts only
      `PROJECTED`; spreads accept both.
    - `per=W` gives Friday closes, like weekly BDH data, and the latest close as the
      last row. `frq=W` would step back seven days at a time from today.
    - `spread(spread_type=OAS)` is null for an index. Use `OAS_SOVEREIGN`, `OAS_SWAP`,
      or `Z` with `universe_type`.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- The same numbers come from BDH:
  `bq.bdh(["I30904EU Index"], ["INDEX_YIELD_TO_WORST", "INDEX_OAS_TSY"], start, end)`.
  `INDEX_OAS_TSY` is the OAS with `RETURNS`, but in percent instead of basis
  points.
- The hedged index `H30904EU` has the same yield and spread; only its returns
  differ.

## Tier 2: spread to call or to maturity

YAS: `spread(price=..., workout=...)`
{ .recipe-uses }

The EUR Tier 2 bonds of SEB, Handelsbanken and Swedbank at today's price: Z-spread
and yield if the bank calls the bond at the first call date, and if it does not.
This is the YAS calculator run from BQL.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#px = px_last();
    #z_call = spread(spread_type=Z, price=#px, workout=TO_NEXT_CALL);
    #z_mat = spread(spread_type=Z, price=#px, workout=TO_MATURITY);
    #y_call = yield(price=#px, workout=TO_NEXT_CALL);
    #y_mat = yield(price=#px, workout=TO_MATURITY);)
get(name, nxt_call_dt, #px, #z_call, #z_mat, #y_call, #y_mat)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['SEB', 'SHBASS', 'SWEDA'] and crncy() == 'EUR' and
           basel_iii_designation() == 'Tier 2'))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(
    df.select(
        "name",
        call="nxt_call_dt",
        price=pl.col("#px").round(2),
        z_call=pl.col("#z_call").round(),
        z_mat=pl.col("#z_mat").round(),
        y_call=pl.col("#y_call").round(2),
        y_mat=pl.col("#y_mat").round(2),
        extension=(pl.col("#z_mat") - pl.col("#z_call")).round(),
    ).sort("call")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (9, 8)
┌─────────────────────┬────────────┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────────┐
│ name                ┆ call       ┆ price  ┆ z_call ┆ z_mat ┆ y_call ┆ y_mat ┆ extension │
│ ---                 ┆ ---        ┆ ---    ┆ ---    ┆ ---   ┆ ---    ┆ ---   ┆ ---       │
│ str                 ┆ date       ┆ f64    ┆ f64    ┆ f64   ┆ f64    ┆ f64   ┆ f64       │
╞═════════════════════╪════════════╪════════╪════════╪═══════╪════════╪═══════╪═══════════╡
│ SWEDA 3 ⅝ 08/23/32  ┆ 2027-08-23 ┆ 99.69  ┆ 85.0   ┆ 196.0 ┆ 4.01   ┆ 5.32  ┆ 110.0     │
│ SHBASS 3 ¼ 06/01/33 ┆ 2028-06-01 ┆ 98.69  ┆ 79.0   ┆ 153.0 ┆ 4.14   ┆ 4.91  ┆ 75.0      │
│ SEB 5 08/17/33      ┆ 2028-08-17 ┆ 101.31 ┆ 83.0   ┆ 159.0 ┆ 4.19   ┆ 4.96  ┆ 75.0      │
│ SHBASS 5 08/16/34   ┆ 2029-08-16 ┆ 101.78 ┆ 91.0   ┆ 151.0 ┆ 4.29   ┆ 4.89  ┆ 59.0      │
│ SEB 4 ½ 11/27/34    ┆ 2029-11-27 ┆ 100.92 ┆ 79.0   ┆ 137.0 ┆ 4.17   ┆ 4.76  ┆ 58.0      │
│ SWEDA 3 ½ 08/19/35  ┆ 2030-08-19 ┆ 96.92  ┆ 103.0  ┆ 111.0 ┆ 4.4    ┆ 4.51  ┆ 8.0       │
│ SWEDA 4 ½ 09/29/36  ┆ 2031-09-29 ┆ 99.83  ┆ 117.0  ┆ 113.0 ┆ 4.54   ┆ 4.54  ┆ -4.0      │
│ SHBASS 3 ⅝ 11/04/36 ┆ 2031-11-04 ┆ 96.19  ┆ 113.0  ┆ 125.0 ┆ 4.5    ┆ 4.66  ┆ 12.0      │
│ SEB 4 08/18/37      ┆ 2032-08-18 ┆ 97.48  ┆ 114.0  ┆ 108.0 ┆ 4.51   ┆ 4.5   ┆ -6.0      │
└─────────────────────┴────────────┴────────┴────────┴───────┴────────┴───────┴───────────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - `price=` takes a number or an expression; `price=#px` runs YAS at `px_last()`.
      `workout=` without `price=` is rejected with "Incorrect parameters provided".
    - `TO_WORST` picks the workout with the lower yield, not the lower spread. A bond
      can be worst to call although its spread to maturity is lower.
    - Without `price=`, `spread()` uses Bloomberg's own pricing source, not
      `px_last()`. Pass the same `price=` to every value you compare.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `workout=` is `TO_WORST` (the default), `TO_NEXT_CALL`, `TO_NEXT_PUT`,
  `TO_MATURITY` or `TO_CUSTOM`. `yield()` and the other spread types take the same
  parameters.
- These bonds reset their coupon to the swap rate plus the original margin if they
  are not called. `extension` is the spread to maturity minus the spread to call.
  When it is positive, the reset margin is above today's market spread and the
  bank saves money by calling. When it is negative, an investor earns less spread
  if the bond is not called.

## One bond at four prices

YAS: `workout=TO_CUSTOM`, `workout_date`
{ .recipe-uses }

The SEB 4 08/18/37 Tier 2 bond, first call 18 August 2032, at four prices:
Z-spread to the call, to a custom date two years later, and to maturity, and the
yield to worst.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

bond = "DO405623 Corp"  # SEB 4 08/18/37, first call 2032-08-18
rows = []
with BQuery() as bq:
    for price in [96, 98, 100, 102]:
        query = f"""
        get(spread(spread_type=Z, price={price}, workout=TO_NEXT_CALL) as #z_call,
            spread(spread_type=Z, price={price}, workout=TO_CUSTOM,
                   workout_date=2034-08-18) as #z_2034,
            spread(spread_type=Z, price={price}, workout=TO_MATURITY) as #z_mat,
            yield(price={price}, workout=TO_WORST) as #ytw)
        for(['{bond}'])
        """
        rows.append(bq.bql(query).combine().with_columns(price=pl.lit(price)))
print(
    pl.concat(rows).select(
        "price",
        z_call=pl.col("#z_call").round(),
        z_2034=pl.col("#z_2034").round(),
        z_mat=pl.col("#z_mat").round(),
        ytw=pl.col("#ytw").round(2),
    )
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (4, 5)
┌───────┬────────┬────────┬───────┬──────┐
│ price ┆ z_call ┆ z_2034 ┆ z_mat ┆ ytw  │
│ ---   ┆ ---    ┆ ---    ┆ ---   ┆ ---  │
│ i32   ┆ f64    ┆ f64    ┆ f64   ┆ f64  │
╞═══════╪════════╪════════╪═══════╪══════╡
│ 96    ┆ 144.0  ┆ 136.0  ┆ 126.0 ┆ 4.68 │
│ 98    ┆ 103.0  ┆ 104.0  ┆ 102.0 ┆ 4.4  │
│ 100   ┆ 63.0   ┆ 73.0   ┆ 78.0  ┆ 4.0  │
│ 102   ┆ 24.0   ┆ 43.0   ┆ 55.0  ┆ 3.61 │
└───────┴────────┴────────┴───────┴──────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `workout=TO_CUSTOM, workout_date=...` assumes the bond is repaid at 100 on that
  date; `workout_price=` sets another redemption price. Use it for a call that
  comes late, or for the date you plan to sell.
- The spread to the nearest date moves most with the price: the gain or loss
  against 100 is spread over fewer years.
- The other direction works too: `price(spread=100, spread_type=Z,
  workout=TO_NEXT_CALL)` is the price for a Z-spread of 100 bp to the call, and
  `price(yield=4.5, workout=TO_NEXT_CALL)` the price for a yield.

## SEK AT1 floaters: discount margin

YAS: `discount_margin(price=...)`
{ .recipe-uses }

The floating rate AT1s in SEK of six Swedish banks: the quoted margin over STIBOR,
the discount margin at today's price, and the discount margin if you pay one point
more.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#px = px_last();)
get(name, nxt_call_dt, #px, flt_spread() as #margin,
    discount_margin(price=#px) as #dm,
    discount_margin(price=#px + 1) as #dm_plus_1)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['SEB', 'SHBASS', 'SBAB', 'LFBANK', 'KLARNA', 'SVEABK'] and
           crncy() == 'SEK' and cpn_typ() == 'FLOATING' and
           basel_iii_designation() == 'Additional Tier 1'))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(
    df.select(
        "name",
        call="nxt_call_dt",
        price=pl.col("#px").round(2),
        margin="#margin",
        dm=pl.col("#dm").round(),
        dm_plus_1=pl.col("#dm_plus_1").round(),
        bp_per_point=(pl.col("#dm") - pl.col("#dm_plus_1")).round(),
    ).sort("call")
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (10, 7)
┌───────────────────┬────────────┬────────┬────────┬───────┬───────────┬──────────────┐
│ name              ┆ call       ┆ price  ┆ margin ┆ dm    ┆ dm_plus_1 ┆ bp_per_point │
│ ---               ┆ ---        ┆ ---    ┆ ---    ┆ ---   ┆ ---       ┆ ---          │
│ str               ┆ date       ┆ f64    ┆ f64    ┆ f64   ┆ f64       ┆ f64          │
╞═══════════════════╪════════════╪════════╪════════╪═══════╪═══════════╪══════════════╡
│ KLARNA Float PERP ┆ 2027-03-25 ┆ 101.5  ┆ 700.0  ┆ 277.0 ┆ 3.0       ┆ 274.0        │
│ SBAB Float PERP   ┆ 2027-04-13 ┆ 100.61 ┆ 320.0  ┆ 166.0 ┆ -79.0     ┆ 245.0        │
│ SVEABK Float PERP ┆ 2028-04-03 ┆ 103.79 ┆ 750.0  ┆ 462.0 ┆ 389.0     ┆ 73.0         │
│ SVEABK Float PERP ┆ 2028-12-20 ┆ 101.5  ┆ 750.0  ┆ 735.0 ┆ 724.0     ┆ 12.0         │
│ LFBANK Float PERP ┆ 2029-01-23 ┆ 102.0  ┆ 290.0  ┆ 195.0 ┆ 148.0     ┆ 47.0         │
│ SBAB Float PERP   ┆ 2029-02-21 ┆ 102.28 ┆ 300.0  ┆ 195.0 ┆ 150.0     ┆ 45.0         │
│ SEB Float PERP    ┆ 2029-09-03 ┆ 101.97 ┆ 280.0  ┆ 206.0 ┆ 169.0     ┆ 37.0         │
│ LFBANK Float PERP ┆ 2030-09-09 ┆ 100.81 ┆ 235.0  ┆ 212.0 ┆ 184.0     ┆ 28.0         │
│ SBAB Float PERP   ┆ 2030-09-23 ┆ 100.59 ┆ 235.0  ┆ 218.0 ┆ 190.0     ┆ 28.0         │
│ SHBASS Float PERP ┆ 2031-04-01 ┆ 100.62 ┆ 235.0  ┆ 219.0 ┆ 195.0     ┆ 25.0         │
└───────────────────┴────────────┴────────┴────────┴───────┴───────────┴──────────────┘
```

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- `flt_spread()` is the quoted margin, the spread the coupon pays over the
  reference rate. `discount_margin(price=100)` is close to it: at par a floater
  earns its margin.
- For these perpetual notes the discount margin is to the next call (`TO_WORST`
  and `TO_NEXT_CALL` give the same value). `workout=TO_MATURITY` changes it.
- `bp_per_point` is the discount margin you give up for each point of price. Close
  to the call date one point costs a lot of margin, so check the call date before
  you pay up for a short floater.
- `price=#px + 1` shows that `price=` takes arithmetic too.

## Pitfalls

What surprised us while writing these recipes.

<div class="recipe-pitfalls" markdown>

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "OAS" numbers match the Z-spread | `spread()` without a type is the Z-spread | `spread(spread_type=OAS)` |
| Each group appears twice after `combine()`, half of the values null | A null group key: `capital_contingent_security()` is null for most non-CoCos, and `combine()` does not join null keys | `if(capital_contingent_security(), true, false)` |
| Grouped items over dates do not join, three times as many rows | `ORIG_IDS` is null in every row | `preferences(dropCols=['ORIG_IDS'])` |
| A monthly history on the 17th of each month | `frq=M` steps back from the end date | `per=M` for month-end closes |
| A weekly history on Tuesdays | `frq=W` steps back seven days from today | `per=W` for Friday closes |
| An index's yield or spread is null | No `universe_type` | `universe_type=PROJECTED` (the only one for yield to worst) or `RETURNS` |
| "Incorrect parameters provided" for `spread()` or `yield()` | `workout=` without `price=` | Add `price=px_last()` or a number |
| The index OAS is 100 times smaller in BDH | `INDEX_OAS_TSY` is in percent, BQL in basis points | Multiply the BDH value by 100 |
| The daily average jumps on a holiday | Fewer bonds are priced that day | Compare the bond count, or use the median |
| Two aliases, one column | BQL merges identical expressions, such as `spread()` and `spread(spread_type=Z)`, into one item | Ask for each expression once |

</div>

!!! abstract "Related"
    See also `YAS <GO>` and `BQLX <GO>`. For how `bql()` and `combine()` work, see
    [BQL](../usage/bql.md).

---

Source: https://marekozana.github.io/polars-bloomberg/recipes/fundamentals/

# Company Fundamentals

A bond has no EBITDA. Often its issuer has none either. Virgin Media O2 issues bonds
through eight vehicles, and the accounts a credit analyst reads belong to none of
them. So before you ask for leverage, you have to find the company that reports
it. BQL's `fundamentalTicker()` does that for bonds and loans.
{ .recipe-lead }

!!! note "Changed in May 2026"
    In May 2026 Bloomberg changed how it chooses that company. It now skips
    financing vehicles and SPVs, and it prefers operating or holding companies with
    current, frequently reported accounts.

!!! info "Data on this page"
    This page starts from bonds, as a credit investor does. It covers European
    high-yield issuers (Virgin Media O2, INEOS, Altice, Telecom Italia, iliad), the
    AT1 issuers SEB, Handelsbanken and Swedbank, and the Bloomberg Pan-European High
    Yield index.

    Amounts are in millions. The outputs below are live data as of 2026-11-17 and will
    differ when you run the queries. Before you adapt a query, read the
    [Pitfalls](#pitfalls).

## Quick reference

=== "By task"

    | You want | Use | One row per |
    |---|---|---|
    | The company whose accounts cover a bond or loan | `fundamentalTicker(<bonds>)` as the universe | company |
    | A company's figure next to each bond | `value(<field>, fundamentalticker, mapby=LINEAGE)` | bond |
    | Annual, half-year, quarterly or LTM figures | `with(fa_period_type=A, fa_period_offset=range(-1Y, 0Y))`, `fpt=S`, `Q`, `LTM` | company and period |
    | Reported or adjusted figures | `fa_adjusted=N` or `Y`; `fa_act_est_data=A` for actuals | company and period |
    | Revenue per business line or country | `segments('<equity>', type=reported, hierarchy=PRODUCT)` or `hierarchy=LOCATION` | segment and period |
    | Bank capital and profitability | `bs_tier1_com_equity_ratio()`, `normalized_roe()` with `fpt=Q` | bank and quarter |
    | A statistic per sector | `median(group(<field>, classification_name(BCLASS, 3)))` over the index's companies | sector |
    | Bloomberg Intelligence's sector figures | `bq.bsrch("BI:TPD", overrides={"BIKEY": ...})` | row of the template |

=== "Period parameters"

    The period parameters work on any fundamental field, either in `with(...)` for the
    whole query or on one field, as in `ebitda(fpt=LTM)`.

    | Parameter | Short | Example values | Meaning |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `fa_period_type` | `fpt` | `A`, `S`, `Q`, `LTM` | annual, half-year, quarter, last twelve months |
    | `fa_period_offset` | `fpo` | `0`, `-1`, `range(-3Q, 0Q)` | periods counted back from the company's latest report |
    | `fa_period_reference` | `fpr` | `2026Q3`, `range(2026Q1, 2026Q3)` | calendar periods, the same for every company |
    | `fa_adjusted` | | `N`, `Y` | as reported, or Bloomberg-adjusted |
    | `fa_act_est_data` | | `A`, `E` | actuals or estimates |
    | `currency` | | `EUR` | the currency of the result; check the `CURRENCY` column |

## From a bond to the company that reports

`value(..., fundamentalticker, mapby=LINEAGE)`
{ .recipe-uses }

For each ticker, the issuing entities of its live bonds, the company whose accounts
`fundamentalTicker` uses, and the capital structure (CAST) parent.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
let(#accounts = value(name, fundamentalticker, mapby=LINEAGE);
    #cast = value(name, parent(type=CAST), mapby=LINEAGE);)
get(ticker, issuer(), #accounts, #cast)
for(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
           ticker in ['VMED', 'INEGRP', 'ALTICE', 'TITIM', 'ILDFP', 'HEIBOS', 'SEB']))
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine(on="ID")
print(
    df.group_by("ticker", "#accounts", "#cast")
    .agg(issuers=pl.col("issuer()").n_unique(), bonds=pl.len())
    .sort("ticker", "bonds", descending=[False, True])
)
```

Output
``` { .text .no-copy .recipe-output }
shape: (8, 5)
┌────────┬───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬─────────┬───────┐
│ ticker ┆ #accounts                     ┆ #cast                         ┆ issuers ┆ bonds │
│ ---    ┆ ---                           ┆ ---                           ┆ ---     ┆ ---   │
│ str    ┆ str                           ┆ str                           ┆ u32     ┆ u32   │
╞════════╪═══════════════════════════════╪═══════════════════════════════╪═════════╪═══════╡
│ ALTICE ┆ Altice International Sarl     ┆ Next Alt Sarl                 ┆ 2       ┆ 6     │
│ HEIBOS ┆ Heimstaden AB                 ┆ Heimstaden AB                 ┆ 2       ┆ 25    │
│ ILDFP  ┆ iliad SA                      ┆ Maya SAS/Paris France         ┆ 1       ┆ 11    │
│ INEGRP ┆ INEOS Group Holdings SA       ┆ INEOS Ltd                     ┆ 1       ┆ 7     │
│ SEB    ┆ Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken ┆ Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken ┆ 2       ┆ 79    │
│ TITIM  ┆ Telecom Italia SpA/Milano     ┆ Poste Italiane SpA            ┆ 3       ┆ 11    │
│ TITIM  ┆ TIM SA/Brazil                 ┆ Poste Italiane SpA            ┆ 1       ┆ 1     │
│ VMED   ┆ VMED O2 UK Holdings Ltd       ┆ Vmed O2 UK Ltd                ┆ 8       ┆ 19    │
└────────┴───────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴─────────┴───────┘
```

!!! warning "Watch out"

    - Heimstaden Bostad bonds map to Heimstaden AB, although Bostad publishes its own
      accounts. For a subsidiary's own figures, query its equity directly:
      `issuerOf('<bond>')` gives `1546973D SS Equity` for Heimstaden Bostad.
    - The projected items add `SOURCE_ID`, so join on `ID`.

Notes
{ .recipe-label }

- Eight Virgin Media O2 vehicles, from Virgin Media Secured Finance to the vendor
  financing DACs, lead to one set of accounts. Bloomberg's own example is INEOS:
  the old logic mapped its bonds to the issuer INEOS Finance plc, the new one maps
  them to INEOS Group Holdings SA.
- `fundamentalTicker` and the CAST parent answer different questions. The CAST
  parent of Telecom Italia is Poste Italiane, its largest shareholder. The accounts
  stay with Telecom Italia, which reports them. The CAST parent is the top of the
  capital structure; `fundamentalTicker` is the company whose figures matter for
  the bond.
- One `TITIM` bond is issued by TIM SA, the Brazilian subsidiary, and maps to TIM's
  own accounts.

## Annual revenue and EBITDA, last two years

`fundamentalticker(...)`, `fa_period_type=A`, `fa_period_offset=range(-1Y, 0Y)`
{ .recipe-uses }

Revenue, EBITDA and EBITDA margin of the high-yield companies above, for the last
two fiscal years, in EUR millions.

```python
import polars as pl
from polars_bloomberg import BQuery

query = """
get(name, sales_rev_turn / 1M as #revenue, ebitda / 1M as #ebitda)
for(fundamentalticker(filter(bondsUniv(ACTIVE, consolidateduplicates=True),
                             ticker in ['VMED', 'INEGRP', 'ALTICE', 'TITIM', 'ILDFP'])))
with(fa_period_type=A, fa_period_offset=range(-1Y, 0Y), currency=EUR)
preferences(dropCols=['AS_OF_DATE', 'REVISION_DATE'])
"""
with BQuery() as bq:
    df = bq.bql(query).combine()
table = df.sort("name", "PERIOD_END_DATE").select(
    "name",
    "PERIOD_END_DATE",
    revenue=pl.col("#revenue").round().cast(pl.Int64),
    ebitda=pl.col("#ebitda").round().cast(pl.Int64),
    margin_pct=(100 * pl.col("#ebitda") / pl.col("#revenue")).round(1),
    ebitda_chg_pct=(100 * pl.col("#ebitda").pct_change().over("name")).round(1),
)
with pl.Config(tbl_rows=20):
    print(table)
```

Output
